description.narrative: (Kenya): Using FY 2022 resources, will support the Kenya Tuberculosis Accelerated Response and Care II (TB-ARC II) activity to provide support at the national and county levels to reduce tuberculosis (TB) incidence and deaths. Major interventions under the activity will include supporting improvements in the quality of existing TB diagnostic and treatment networks, strengthening services to accommodate a larger number of patients, and increasing case identification of TB, TB/HIV, and Drug Resistant-TB, including amongst children. The activity will enhance the efficiency and sustainability of the Kenya National Tuberculosis Program by building on the existing national treatment platforms and working to further increase the timely use of quality TB treatment services. The activity contributes to the attainment of U.S. Embassy Nairobi's Integrated Country Strategy Goal 3 of promoting a healthy, educated and productive Kenyan population to drive inclusive and sustainable development in the health sector. The activity will also provide technical assistance for local adaptation and scale-up of globally proven interventions, and will strengthen monitoring and evaluation of TB, and TB/HIV control interventions. Infectious disease prevention, detection and response is a priority U.S. security concerns as such diseases could spread beyond Kenya's borders. This activity also closely works with Kenyan TB experts, building their respective capacities and commitment to better plan and implement Kenya-led TB programs. This activity is also receiving HIV funds $1,022,001 in COP22..
